part.text:
Fixed. In `to_json` for enums (include/nlohmann/detail/conversions/to_json.hpp:4405 and the same spot in single_include/nlohmann/json.hpp:5694), the single enum overload now dispatches on the underlying type:

- unsigned underlying type → `number_unsigned` construction (so `2^63` serializes as `9223372036854775808`, not a negative number)
- signed or default underlying type → `number_integer` construction (unchanged behavior)

Validation:
- `test-udt_cpp11` (contains the FAIL_TO_PASS large-unsigned-enum checks): 11/11 test cases, 70/70 assertions pass
- `test-conversions_cpp11`, `test-iterators2_cpp11`, `test-serialization_cpp11`: all pass
- Standalone C++11/C++17 checks against both the multi-header and amalgamated single-header pass (round-trip `get<book_id>()`, signed enums still negative, plain enums still integer)
- `test-regression2` build failures are pre-existing on the pristine tree (verified via stash) and unrelated to this change
